chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Byeong Fire is the sun, and you love the fun parts: the spark, the late calls, the inside jokes nobody else gets. A situationship can be all highlights and no responsibility, and honestly that's enjoyable for a while. You stay because when it's good, it's really good. But suns need warmth back too. If you've noticed you're giving more energy than you're getting, the fun can start to feel like a performance you're putting on twice a week. Ask yourself: if the fun nights stopped tomorrow, what would actually be left between you?
text.what-you-want: You know what you want, and you've probably already joked about it. Byeong Fire tends to say the true thing as a joke so it doesn't land too heavily. Haha, so are we dating or what. Try saying it without the haha. You want to be seen and celebrated, chosen in public and not only enjoyed in private. You want someone who's proud to stand next to your light. That's a completely reasonable thing to want, and you're allowed to want it now rather than at some vague point in the future.
text.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you probably turn up the warmth: more plans, more energy, more charm, as if clarity were a prize you could win. Byeong Fire tries to shine brighter. It rarely works, because clarity isn't something you earn by performing. It's something they either offer or don't. Instead of increasing your output, try matching theirs for a week. Not as a game or a test. Just to see the real level of effort in this thing when you're not the one carrying all of it on your back.
text.the-talk: Your talk will be warm and honest, which is great. The risk is making it big. Byeong Fire can turn a simple question into a speech with three acts and a callback. Keep it short, in an ordinary setting, not at a party or in front of friends. Something like: I'm having fun, and I want to know if this is going somewhere. I'd like it to. What about you? Then let there be silence. Silence is not a fire you need to put out with more words. Let them fill it.
text.your-line: Your line is being hidden. Byeong Fire cannot live in the shadows. If you're kept away from their friends, left off their life when you'd like to be part of it, or only ever seen late at night, notice it and name it to yourself. Decide where your line is. When it's crossed, step back without a scene, and without a long explanation post. Your light deserves someone who's openly glad to stand next to it in daylight, in front of the people they love. Notice, too, how often you've made excuses for them to friends. That habit is usually the first sign your line has already moved.
text.either-way: Either way, you keep your light. If they want more, wonderful, and let them show it with effort, not only words. If not, you'll be sad, honestly sad, and then you'll be out with friends and laughing far sooner than you expect. Byeong Fire is wonderfully resilient. Just don't sprint to the next spark before you understand why this one didn't catch. One quiet evening of thinking it through will save you from repeating the same lovely, exhausting pattern with someone new. Write three lines about what you learned, then go dancing. Both parts matter, in that order.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: When it's good, it's so good. I get it, Byeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And when it's not, you just shine harder. Exhausting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say what you want without the joke.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Drop the 'haha'. It's doing a lot of heavy lifting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You deserve someone proud to be seen with you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Daylight test. Do you only exist to them after 10pm?

spring.intro: A spring sun rises with fuel to spare. Wood ruled your birth season and feeds your Fire, so you approach a situationship with optimism: it's fun, it's fine, it'll turn into something. You probably light up every hangout and make the in-between feel warmer than it is. That generosity is beautiful and slightly convenient for them. Why define anything when the sun shows up regardless? Spring Byeong's habit is assuming warmth will grow a relationship on its own. Warmth helps. Roots need commitment. Ask yourself whether they've done anything to earn the morning light, or whether you simply rise anyway.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You'd rise for them even if they never asked. They know that, Byeong.

summer.intro: A summer-born sun runs at full blaze. Fire ruled your season and doubled your element, so you're intense, generous and very visible. In a situationship that heat cuts both ways. You make it feel like the most exciting thing in their week, and then you get bored, run hot and cold, or blow it up with one dramatic message. Summer Byeong often keeps things undefined because a label feels like a smaller sky. Be honest: is the vagueness their choice or yours? If it's yours, own it out loud. If it's theirs, you deserve someone who wants to stand in your light on purpose.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Is it vague because of them, or because a label shrinks your sky?

autumn.intro: Autumn Byeong is a sun with work to do. Metal ruled your birth season, and Fire's role is to shape Metal, so you tend to treat love as something to build. In a situationship you might be trying to forge it into a relationship by sheer effort: being perfect company, solving their problems, proving you're worth choosing. It's admirable and exhausting. You can't hammer someone into commitment. The autumn sun's strength is clear, golden light. Use it to look honestly at what's there: what they offer, unprompted, week after week. That's the real shape of this. Decide from that shape, not from what you hope to make of it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Being perfect company every week isn't a job interview. Stop auditioning, Byeong.

winter.intro: A winter sun learns early that warmth can be taken away. Water ruled your birth season, Byeong, and Water is the element that dims Fire, so beneath all your brightness sits a worry about being too much and getting cooled down. In a situationship that worry becomes rules: don't double text, don't ask, don't show how much you care. You keep it light so nobody can douse you. But hiding your heat is still being doused, just by yourself. Winter Byeong's honest move is to let one ray through. Tell them you like them. If that cools them off, they were never going to warm your winter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your warmth isn't too much, Byeong. Let one honest ray through.

strength.strong: Your fire is well fed, Byeong, so you shine without trying. In a situationship you probably run the energy: the plans, the fun, the conversation. It's great, and it can drown them out. Some people go quiet next to a strong sun and never get to show what they'd bring. The blind spot is mistaking your enthusiasm for mutual momentum. Turn it down slightly and see whether they step forward. If they do, lovely. If they don't, you've learned something important without having to force a single conversation about it.
strength.weak: With little to feed your flame, Byeong, you keep shining partly to be noticed. In a situationship you might be working hard to stay entertaining and easy, worried that asking for more would end the fun. You give warmth and take scraps. The blind spot is shrinking your needs to keep your place. You're allowed to want the boring parts of love: plans, labels, reliability. They aren't less romantic. Tell them what you need, and let them show you whether they can match even half your warmth.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practise clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyse every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analysed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: Firewood for a sun that forgets to look down
gap-wood.text: A Gap Wood in a situationship is steady in a way you might not notice until you look for it. They show up. They remember the name of your boss. They drive you home after the party you dragged them to and don't complain about the parking. You bring the light; Gap brings the logs. The trouble is that logs are easy to take for granted when you're busy being a sun. The drift tends to start in your texting. You go dark for a day because life got loud, then come back with a flood of caps lock and a sunset photo. To you that's normal. To Gap, the silence looked like a step back, and they may have quietly counted it. Gap rarely complains out loud. Gap just goes a little more formal, and that formality is your signal to read. For the talk, Gap wants something concrete, so give them a sentence they can hold: I'm not just having fun with you. I'd like this to be a proper thing. Are you in? Then ask what they need from you, and actually listen to the answer without turning it into a party. Asking is the part suns usually skip.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, the logs don't chop themselves. Say thank you out loud.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, stop counting the silent hours and just say what you need.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Warm talk, short talk. No slides.

eul-wood.title: Bloom season at the far end of the table
eul-wood.text: An Eul Wood makes you feel like the sun, which is your favourite feeling. Eul laughs at your stories, follows your plans, turns up at the bar you picked and makes friends with everyone you know. It's effortless, and that's the risk. When something is this easy, you can stop looking at it. The drift happens while you're busy shining. You're the centre of the evening, Eul is at the edge of it, and you don't notice the edge getting quieter. Eul's signals are soft: a slightly shorter reply, a story you're clearly meant to see, a mention of someone who asked them out. You might call that playing games. More often it's Eul trying to be seen without making a scene. Your signals are loud and many, a dozen heart emojis, a 9 p.m. call, and also a plan you forgot about by Thursday. For the talk, make it about Eul, not about the fun. One thoughtful message lands better than ten bright ones: I don't just love hanging out with you. I want you to be my person. How do you feel? Then remember what Eul says. Every word. Eul remembers everything, so match that.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, the flower is turning towards you. Look down once in a while.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, the strategic story post is not a conversation.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say 'I miss you' plainly. Both of you.

byeong-fire.title: Two suns, one spotlight
byeong-fire.text: Two Byeong Fires in a situationship look, from the outside, like the most fun couple at every party. You both know everyone. You both tell stories with sound effects. Your chat is caps lock, voice notes recorded on the street, and video calls from queues. It is a lot of light. The drift hides in the brightness. With two suns, there's only one spotlight, and without noticing you start taking turns in it rather than sharing it. You tell a story, they top it. They plan a birthday, you plan a better one. Neither of you is great at listening slowly, so the deeper question of what this is gets crowded out by the next plan. You also both crash after big weeks, sometimes at the same time, and suddenly the chat that never stopped goes quiet on both ends. Each of you reads the other's silence as cooling off. For the talk, pick a quiet place, no friends, no music, no audience. One of you asks a real question and the other answers it slowly: Are we doing this properly? Because I want to. No jokes until the answer is out. Then celebrate. You're both very good at that part.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two suns. Every party is better with you two in it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And neither of you has listened for longer than a minute.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Quiet room, real question, slow answer. Then dance.

jeong-fire.title: Message number thirty-nine
jeong-fire.text: A Jeong Fire is your kind of person and a completely different kind of fire. You light up a whole street; Jeong lights up one room and stays lit long after you've gone home. With Jeong, the conversations go deeper than you usually let them, and you like who you are in that candlelight. The drift in this pair is about focus. You reply to forty people a day. Jeong notices if their message was number thirty-nine. Jeong can see you at a party being generous with everyone and quietly wonder if they're special or just included. You might find Jeong's questions intense, and Jeong might find your breeziness hard to read. When you argue, it flares fast on both sides, and you've forgotten it by breakfast while Jeong remembers every word. Your signal is warmth spread wide, which can feel to Jeong like not being chosen. For the talk, give Jeong focus, not volume. One message, not ten. In person, quietly: You're not one of my many people. You're the one I want. Can we stop pretending this is casual? Then reply to Jeong first for a while. It's the smallest gesture, and to a candle it is very visible.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Same element, different rooms. The sun and the candle.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, reply to Jeong first. It's not hard. It's a choice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, assume warmth. Then ask clearly.

mu-earth.title: Twelve messages, one sincere sentence
mu-earth.text: A Mu Earth is sunlight's favourite mountain: solid, calm, quietly impressive. You warm them up and they make you feel steady. With Mu, you sleep better. That's not nothing for a sun. The drift in this situationship comes from tempo. You text a lot: plans, jokes, a photo of the sky, an idea for Saturday, a better idea for Saturday. Mu replies once, with one sincere sentence, sometimes hours later. You start to wonder if they're bored. More likely, Mu just doesn't do volume. You also want to go out and celebrate things; Mu wants to stay in and order the same curry. After a few weeks of you suggesting and Mu declining, it can feel like you're doing all the running. When you push, you get louder, and Mu goes still and immovable, which makes you louder still. Your signal is energy, which can feel to Mu like pressure. For the talk, count quality, not quantity. Then ask calmly, maybe on one of Mu's stay-in nights: I like you, and I'd like us to be official. Would you want that? Let Mu answer slowly. A mountain's yes doesn't come with fireworks, but it tends to hold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, a quick 'haha' keeps the sun shining. Cheap, effective.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, twelve texts to one reply is just Mu's exchange rate. Accept it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Count quality, not quantity. That one sentence was sincere.

gi-earth.title: Sunshine and the forgotten errand
gi-earth.text: Things grow when a Byeong Fire shines on a Gi Earth, and you can feel it. Gi makes your life work better: they remember your dentist, check you got home, turn your chaotic plan into an actual booking. You make Gi laugh, take them places, warm up their careful world. It's a good match, and it's also very easy to take for granted from your side. The drift in this situationship tends to be in the details. You promise to come to Gi's friend's thing and forget. You say 'let's do a weekend away' and then nothing happens until Gi books it. Gi notices every forgotten thing, and Gi worries, and when Gi mentions it, you might call it negativity. That's where Gi stops mentioning things. Gi might start feeling like the one who cleans up after the sun, and you might start feeling nagged. Your signal is enthusiasm, which can look like promises without follow-through. For the talk, show Gi it's not just fun to you: I don't just love being with you, I want to show up properly. Can we make this real? Then answer Gi's questions, the practical ones especially. That's how Gi hears 'I'm serious'.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sun on the garden. Things genuinely grow here.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, answer Gi's questions. Yes, the boring ones.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, enjoy the sunshine without auditing it.

gyeong-metal.title: Caps lock versus 'ok.'
gyeong-metal.text: A Gyeong Metal is a challenge, and you like a challenge. They don't melt at your charm, and that's half the attraction. When Gyeong finally laughs at your joke, it feels like you've won something. The drift in this situationship runs hot. You want warmth, celebration and enthusiasm back. Gyeong wants results and respect, and gives warmth in a dry, practical way that you might not recognise. You send a message bursting with emojis about your promotion; Gyeong replies 'nice. well deserved.' You take it personally. Gyeong meant it neutrally, possibly even as high praise. When you push for more heat, Gyeong digs in, and when Gyeong is blunt, your mood dims. Then it's a fight, and you both want the last word. Fighting by text is the worst version: your caps lock against Gyeong's one-word replies. The question of what you are gets lost in the sparks. Your signal is intensity, which can feel to Gyeong like pressure. For the talk, do it in person, no audience, no texting it out: I like you, and I'd like us to be together properly. Where are you? Agree, together, that short doesn't mean cold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, Gyeong's 'nice' was high praise. Truly.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Never fight by text. Caps lock versus 'ok.' is a disaster.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, one warm word out loud. It costs a second.

sin-metal.title: Everyone thinks you're a couple already
sin-metal.text: 丙 and 辛 is a heavenly combination: sunlight on a jewel. You make Sin sparkle and Sin makes you feel admired by someone with real taste. When it works, people notice you as a pair, even before you've decided you are one. That's the funny part of this situationship: everyone else seems to know what it is except the two of you. The drift happens through small burns. You make a careless joke about Sin's outfit in front of friends. You forget the restaurant Sin mentioned twice. You're loud when Sin wanted a quiet evening. Sin doesn't always say it. Sin tends to withdraw, reply a little later, or turn quietly sharp. You might find Sin's standards picky. Sin might find your attention scattered. Sin's texts are beautifully written and a bit delayed; yours are frequent and excited. Your signal is warmth, but it can feel careless to someone who notices everything. For the talk, notice the effort first. Sin usually puts real thought into how they look and what they say, so name it. Then: I don't want to be the fun person in your life. I want to be your person. Can we make it official? Choose somewhere quiet, with good lighting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 丙辛, sunlight on a jewel. Everyone already thinks you're a couple.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, that joke about Sin's outfit in front of friends? Noted. Forever.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, reply a little faster. The sun notices.

im-water.title: Who sets first over the ocean
im-water.text: An Im Water is the ocean you can't stop looking at. Deep, clever, a bit mysterious, and so different from you that every conversation feels like a discovery. You want to be in it all the time. Im wants to be in it on Im's own tide. The drift in this pair is about distance. You text constantly. Im texts in bursts, or not at all for a day while they think something through. You take the silence as rejection and push harder, a call, a voice note, a 'hello??' with two question marks. Im can feel flooded and step further back, and that looks like more rejection to you. Meanwhile Im's moods can dim your joy, and your need for attention can grate on Im's independence. The 'what are we' question becomes a test you both seem to be failing. Your signal is intensity, and to an ocean it can feel like a storm. For the talk, let silence be silence first. Don't fill every gap. Then ask calmly: I like you a lot and I want to know where we stand. Could this be a relationship? Agree on one daily ping. Then actually believe in the quiet between them.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, silence is just Im thinking. Let it be silence.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, one daily ping. A dot counts. Send the dot.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Ocean and sun. Magnificent, once you agree on the tides.

gye-water.title: Rainbow weather and the badly timed joke
gye-water.text: Sunshine and drizzle make rainbows, and with a Gye Water, you get some of the most beautiful weather of your life. Gye notices things about you nobody else does. They send you a song with no explanation, and you realise later it was exactly about you. The drift in this situationship comes from volume. You're loud, quick, funny, and you joke your way through tension. Gye is quieter, slower to reply, and when Gye shares something tender and you answer with a joke, Gye can feel brushed off. That's the usual spark. You meant to lighten the mood. Gye heard 'this isn't serious to me'. Then Gye goes quiet, you take the quiet as disinterest, you push, and the weather turns. Your signal is brightness, which can feel like overwhelm to someone who needs to hear themselves think. For the talk, turn the volume down. No jokes in the first two minutes. Ask softly, in a calm place: I really like you. I want to be with you properly. What do you want? Then give Gye space to answer, even if it takes until tomorrow. A quiet answer can still be a full one.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sunshine and drizzle. This is rainbow weather.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, no jokes for two minutes. You can do it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, one heart emoji says 'still here'. Send it.
